ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a human reviewer: (1) safety — send the chat log (rider's route query F8, driver's "Shut up and let me drive." F9) for Ryde code-of-conduct review under SAFE-1; (2) fare — confirm the unexempt detour mileage of $7.25 (5.14 km × $1.4102/km) as a Ryde voucher under NS-7 / RD-2 once safety is cleared.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen is the reason this case cannot be decided automatically. The rider's complaint says the driver "told me to shut up" and that she "felt unsafe," and the chat record confirms it: the rider asked "Why are we going this way? This is not the route on the app." at 09:04 [F8], and the driver replied "Shut up and let me drive." at 09:05 [F9]. That is hostile language aimed at the passenger during a live trip — abuse of a kind barred by Ryde's code of conduct, which "will not be tolerated" — so the screen is at least "suspected" under SAFE-1. No threat, intimidation, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears elsewhere in the record [F11][F12][F13][F14][F15]. Under SAFE-1 a suspected safety concern takes the case out of automated adjudication and sends it to a human, so I do not issue a refund.

The routing facts themselves are settled: one off-route segment ran 09:00–09:11, 6.89 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.75 km, +5.14 km, up to 1481 m off route [F3], against a whole-trip overrun of +5.5 km / +35% [F1]. Under RD-1 that is an unexempt detour unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it. RD-4 fails — no traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window [F14], and the PIE band 5 and KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY band 4 speed records [F12][F13] are neither band 1 nor 2 and, per the trace, cannot exempt a segment alone. RD-5 also fails: the complete, fully timestamped chat contains no rider message before 09:00 agreeing to any route [F8][F10] — the only pre-segment message is an objection, not consent — and the driver's post-trip claim that the GPS rerouted him [F11] is a statement, not rider consent (RD-5, G11). No rider-named stop appears, so RD-3(a) does not apply. The segment therefore counts under RD-2.

Had the safety screen been clear, the metered RydeTAXI fare would make the refund $30.22 ÷ 21.43 km = $1.4102/km [F4][F7], and 5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.25 to the cent [F3]; the $0.11 meter waiting time is not refunded under RD-3(c) [F5]. The fare record is internally consistent (base $3.90 + distance $30.22 + time $8.47 + waiting $0.11 + platform $1.47 = $44.17) [F6][F7]. RD-6 does not apply: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so no account flag is issued [F17]. The record on routing is itself sufficient [F3][F4][F10]; the escalation ground is the SAFE-1 screen, and the human reviewer should read F8–F9 and confirm the detour amount under RD-2 / NS-7.
